title: Relative obesity likelihood: low vs high 'activity inequality' countries (index)
geography: World (country groupings from the 2017 Stanford activity study)

source.name: Large-scale physical activity data reveal worldwide activity inequality (Althoff et al.)

notes: 'Activity inequality' = the gap in step counts between a country's most-active and least-active people, distinct from the country's raw average. The study found this gap -- not average step count -- was the strongest predictor of obesity: people in high-inequality countries (e.g. US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Egypt) were found to be almost 200% more likely to be obese than people in low-inequality countries (e.g. Sweden, Japan). Shown here as an index: low-inequality baseline = 100, high-inequality = ~297 (100 + ~197%).

points.label: High activity-inequality countries (e.g. US, Canada, Egypt)
